title: The last digest of the term
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The last digest of the college year. The cover is the classroom, empty, the board wiped, one chair at the back turned toward the door. The tech runs it slow. The owner puts it at the front. The rack has a front now.

panels.composition: The cover: an empty classroom, the board wiped, rows of chairs, one at the back turned to face the door.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing an empty classroom with a wiped board and one chair at the back turned toward the door, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The print shop. The TECH running it, the light sweeping slow. WOOD. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a print technician running a copier slowly while a young man and a small dog wait at the counter, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner putting it at the front of the rack, ahead of the realtor's flyer.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner placing a small booklet at the very front of a wire rack ahead of the other flyers, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The rack. The front. The digest in it. The strip has a front now. It didn't ask for it; it was given.

image.prompt: close on a wire rack with a small booklet placed first in front of a real-estate flyer and a church bulletin, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The rack has a front now. Given, not asked for.
